clue.text: Dancers: all in Sabre Dance

indicators.note: dance asks the letters of the preceding words to move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that every dancer takes part in Khachaturian's famous Sabre Dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sabre Dance' reads as the title of Khachaturian's ballet piece, but 'Dance' is the anagram signal working on ALL IN SABRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet's female performers are its best-known dancers, so the plural fits 'Dancers'.

clue.text: Conservative is restricted by most of grave error

indicators.note: restricted by says the preceding pieces are held inside the word that follows
most of means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: grave and solemn are synonyms for serious

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is hemmed in by a very serious mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' reads as a burial place, but here it means serious; 'most of' and 'restricted by' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a grammatical blunder or breach of etiquette, a kind of mistake.

clue.text: A spicy dish cheers man

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as cheers is
a man is a male

explanation.surface: Someone toasts a man over a hot plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British for 'thank you', like 'cheers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican dish of seasoned meat wrapped in maize dough, often spiced with chilli.

clue.text: Booby-trapped ground, we hear, with care

indicators.note: we hear says the spoken form of the preceding words is what counts

parts.note: ground laid with explosives is mined ground

explanation.surface: Treading carefully over a minefield.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind is to be bothered about something, as in 'I don't mind'.

clue.text: One Ian Craven undergoes a change, hence not displaying this?

definitions.text: One Ian Craven undergoes a change, hence not displaying this?

parts.note: one is written as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: undergoes a change says the letters of the named man are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Ian Craven goes through a transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: whoever changes is then not showing constancy, the quality of never changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Invariance is the property of staying constant, which something that has just changed lacks.

clue.text: Hardy heroine about the last word in insipidity?

indicators.note: about says the heroine's name goes around the next piece

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's best-known heroine
amen is the word said at the very end of a prayer

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy's heroine gives the final verdict on dullness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last word' looks like a phrase for the best example, but it is AMEN, the closing word of a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipidity is a lack of spirit or flavour; docility and lack of excitement come close, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Ill-feeling engendered by vermin kidnapping a student

indicators.note: kidnapping means the vermin hold the following letters inside them

parts.note: mice are household vermin
L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: Resentment caused by rats or mice making off with a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is spite or ill will, a desire to harm someone.

clue.text: Simple game readily yields it

indicators.note: yields says the run of letters comes out of the words game readily

explanation.surface: A straightforward game gives way without a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, plain or simple, as in 'a mere child'.

clue.text: Great homage for business share

parts.note: ado means fuss or palaver, as in 'what a business'
a ration is one's allotted share

explanation.surface: Paying deep respect in exchange for a stake in a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business' sounds commercial but means a fuss, ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship, the highest form of homage.

clue.text: Top secretary accepted by expert very quickly

indicators.note: accepted by says the secretary goes inside the expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a PA, personal assistant, is a senior secretary

explanation.surface: A leading secretary taken on by a specialist in no time.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means at a fast speed, swiftly.

clue.text: Pull fish backward into sheltered side of boat

indicators.note: backward turns the whole run of the two pieces around

parts.note: to draw is to pull
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Hauling a fish backwards into the lee of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAW + EEL read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side faces away from the wind, so it is the sheltered side.

clue.text: Fish that's healthy, according to Cockney mate

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the H at the start of a word, so this signals the dropped letter

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty
a wife is a mate, a spouse

explanation.surface: A Cockney declares a certain fish good for you, mate.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the London East End accent, famous for dropping the H, so HALE comes out as ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North Atlantic herring-like fish.

clue.text: Some hitch hiker AI services — gets lift

indicators.note: some says only part of the words that follow is wanted

explanation.surface: A hitch-hiker at a motorway service station gets a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, with service stations; the 1 serves as an I in the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it up.

clue.text: Nasty behaviour needs reforming, steeped in repellent crimes

indicators.note: steeped in puts the reworked needs inside the reworked crimes
repellent, driving apart, scatters the letters of the synonym for crimes

parts.note: sins are wrongdoings, crimes

indicators.note: reforming asks for the letters of needs to be formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Something in need of reform, soaked in disgusting wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'reforming' and 'repellent' are anagram signals, the second working on the synonym for crimes; 'steeped in' sets one result within the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Snideness is sly, sneering spitefulness, a mean manner.

clue.text: Suspicious behaviour leads to prisons or ultimately — ultimately — hanging

parts.note: sus is British slang for suspicion or suspicious conduct
pens are enclosures, places of confinement

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word repeated after it

explanation.surface: A suspect's conduct leads to prison or, in the end, the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: SUS is British slang (the old 'sus law' let police stop suspects).
explanation.definitionFit: Suspensory describes something that holds up or supports, as a hanging part does.

clue.text: Teams give more — two-thirds of leg completed (i. e. leg not over?)

parts.note: sides are teams
to add is to give more

indicators.note: two-thirds of takes the first two of the three letters of leg

explanation.surface: Teams put in extra effort with two-thirds of a race stage done.
explanation.walkthrough: Riding side-saddle, the rider's leg does not go over the horse's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Side-saddle riding keeps both legs on one side of the horse, so neither crosses it.

clue.text: Poet's denial of individualism, correcting statement about Irish Sea?

explanation.surface: A poem's line against individualism, recast as a geographic correction.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne's line; read as 'No, Man is an island' it corrects the claim that the Irish Sea is one, since the Isle of Man sits in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Donne's meditation says nobody is self-sufficient; it also reads as a correction naming the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Unexpectedly Larry won by a short head

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of Larry won come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Larry's horse won by the smallest margin, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To win narrowly is to win by the slimmest margin, as a horse wins by a short head.

clue.text: Drink that's suitable if bottling anger up?

indicators.note: bottling means the suitable word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: apt means suitable

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word for anger is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Is a drink fitting if you are keeping your rage in check?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' signals reading upwards; 'bottling' is the container signal, like keeping anger bottled up.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Take the place of excellent top player, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the preceding words are to be taken as spoken

parts.note: super means excellent and a seed is a top-ranked tennis player

explanation.surface: Replacing a brilliant leading player, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede is to replace or supplant something.

clue.text: Station-worker farther to the left?

explanation.surface: A railway employee placed further to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the left side of a ship, so 'more port' reads as farther left.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway luggage carrier works at a station; read as more port, it means further to a ship's left.

clue.text: Goggles — Schwarzenegger's foremost muscles

indicators.note: foremost picks the first letter of the name

parts.note: pecs are the chest muscles, pectorals

explanation.surface: Arnold Schwarzenegger's most prominent features are his eyewear and his chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Specs is slang for spectacles, glasses worn over the eyes.

clue.text: Mostly angry argument leads to unhappiness

indicators.note: mostly means the synonym loses its last letter

parts.note: sore can mean angry or aggrieved
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A cross quarrel ends in misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow is grief or sadness.

clue.text: Rouses one with a shake-this is important

indicators.note: with a shake suggests the letters are jolted into another order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is woken roughly because the matter is urgent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serious is grave and weighty, demanding attention.

clue.text: Indifferent call for help attracts nothing

parts.note: SOS is the distress call
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A distress signal draws no response.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Sailor, embarrassed to embrace one, waited

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor

indicators.note: to embrace says the word for embarrassed holds the next piece

parts.note: an embarrassed person is red in the face
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A blushing sailor hesitates to hug someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or delay.

clue.text: Some crotchety person may be a 'character'

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grumpy individual may be described as quite a character.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'may be a'; those are link words, and 'character' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a kind of person, and a character, as in 'a bit of a type'.

clue.text: Odds on English getting a couple of fifties in innings

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds on a horse
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them

explanation.surface: Betting on England to score two half-centuries in their batting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'innings' sounds like cricket, but it is the definition: a spell, a period of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period of activity, as an innings is one's turn or time.

clue.text: Criminal charge and court proceedings including nothing about predatory activities

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

indicators.note: including means the trial word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a trial is court proceedings
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An accused faces a charge and a trial over predatory behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Raptorial describes birds of prey and other animals adapted to seizing prey.
